purpose: Test whether reducing llama.cpp context allocation allows the same 8B CRAFT request to finish on the available GPU. No language comparison.
question: Can the pinned Qwen3-8B CRAFT setup complete two turns and deliver the Director messages when the server reserves a 4,096-token single-slot context instead of 8,192?
prior_observation: v0.20 processed one 512-token prompt batch in 222.30 s then stopped reporting progress for over five minutes; no model response completed.

model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; 99 GPU layers; context 4,096; one parallel slot; logical batch 1,024; physical micro-batch 256; reasoning off; upstream Director/Builder sampling settings

design.communication_condition: CRAFT upstream natural-language prompts and messages with bracket-preserving parser fallback
design.context_policy: No prompt truncation or summarization. If the request exceeds available context, record the backend error and stop.

primary: request completion status and wall time
generated, parsed, and Builder-delivered messages per turn

predictions: The first Director response will complete in under ten minutes.
If the task completes both turns, at least two of three messages will be delivered in each turn.
stop_rule: Stop before issuing another completion if one request has no increase in prompt-processed tokens or decoded tokens for five continuous minutes. Report partial state as a runtime failure, not a task result.
analysis: Publish all complete and partial attempts, with each failure reason. No protocol comparison is triggered by this feasibility run.
